summary: Indian High Commissioner Dinesh Trivedi stated that the PM will receive the highest honor and a memorable reception if he visits India.

caption:
India is ready to give the Bangladesh PM a 'memorable welcome' with the highest honor.

Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Dinesh Trivedi, has stated that if the Prime Minister of Bangladesh visits India, he will be given a memorable welcome with the highest honor.

Trivedi made these remarks during a business reception hosted by the High Commission of India in Dhaka.

He emphasized that while it is important not to forget the past, one should not remain stuck in it, suggesting a forward-looking approach to bilateral relations.

The statement signals India's eagerness to strengthen diplomatic ties and welcome the current leadership of Bangladesh.

headline: Interpol red notice sought for former army chief Aziz Ahmed
summary: The ICT Chief Prosecutor's Office has requested an Interpol red notice to secure the arrest of the retired general accused of crimes against humanity.
details: The Chief Prosecutor’s Office of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) has requested Bangladesh’s National Central Bureau (NCB) to secure an Interpol red notice against former army chief Gen (retd) Aziz Ahmed.
Aziz Ahmed is an accused in a crimes against humanity case involving the 2013 crackdown on Hefazat activists at Motijheel’s Shapla Chattar and in Narayanganj on May 5-6.
Last month, ICT-2 took cognisance of formal charges of genocide and crimes against humanity against ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, two journalists, and 38 others in the same case.
Following the charges, the court issued arrest warrants for 30 absconding accused, including Gen (retd) Aziz Ahmed.
Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam confirmed that his office has established that Aziz is currently living abroad, prompting the request for international assistance in his arrest.
caption:
A former army chief is now facing an international manhunt. The ICT is seeking an Interpol red notice for Gen (retd) Aziz Ahmed.

The Chief Prosecutor’s Office of the International Crimes Tribunal (ICT) has requested Bangladesh’s National Central Bureau (NCB) to secure an Interpol red notice against former army chief Gen (retd) Aziz Ahmed.

Aziz Ahmed is an accused in a crimes against humanity case involving the 2013 crackdown on Hefazat activists at Motijheel’s Shapla Chattar and in Narayanganj on May 5-6.

Last month, ICT-2 took cognisance of formal charges of genocide and crimes against humanity against ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, two journalists, and 38 others in the same case.

Following the charges, the court issued arrest warrants for 30 absconding accused, including Gen (retd) Aziz Ahmed.

Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam confirmed that his office has established that Aziz is currently living abroad, prompting the request for international assistance in his arrest.
